techniques.title: Route by reader task
techniques.problem: Readers with different goals all enter through the same homepage.
techniques.practice: Lead with the common task and offer concise routes for other roles, platforms, or access levels.
techniques.outcome: A first-time reader can choose a route without reading the whole page.

techniques.title: Show a recognizable first result
techniques.problem: Setup commands end without telling the reader what success looks like.
techniques.practice: Pair the first real task with a visible artifact, output, or milestone a new user can recognize.
techniques.outcome: The reader can distinguish success from a partial run.

techniques.title: Execute the documented walkthrough
techniques.problem: Quick-start snippets drift away from the supported build.
techniques.practice: Extract the documented commands and run them from a clean checkout at the advertised ref. Verify the inputs, outputs, and supported platform.
techniques.outcome: A run receipt proves that the actual published commands worked at a named ref.

techniques.title: Show separate platform commands
techniques.problem: Shell syntax, paths, or launchers vary across supported environments.
techniques.practice: Present copyable commands with their platform and shell next to the relevant prerequisites.
techniques.outcome: A reader can copy the appropriate block without translating it.

techniques.title: Link authoritative agent instructions
techniques.problem: An agent starts in product documentation and may miss repository-specific workflow rules.
techniques.practice: Give the README a short route to the applicable AGENTS.md or equivalent and keep policy in that canonical file.
techniques.outcome: The agent can find the correct instructions before making changes.

techniques.title: Label the scope of compatibility evidence
techniques.problem: Readers may assume a development check applies to a published release.
techniques.practice: Label compatibility with the version or ref, platform, feature, and actual verification scope.
techniques.outcome: The reader can tell which combinations have evidence.

techniques.title: Separate drafting, archiving, and publication
techniques.problem: Editing the homepage directly makes acceptance and release history hard to reconstruct.
techniques.practice: Use versioned workspaces, freeze accepted files, and record a distinct homepage publication change.
techniques.outcome: A reader can determine the candidate, accepted archive, and current homepage independently.

techniques.title: Name the collection alongside the version
techniques.problem: Product, homepage, and template versions can have the same number.
techniques.practice: Tag each version with its project and collection and index the collections independently.
techniques.outcome: A reader can identify which artifact a version refers to.

techniques.title: Pin archive bytes to source evidence
techniques.problem: An archive can change silently or lose its source context.
techniques.practice: Record the full source commit and content digest for the frozen README and companion assets.
techniques.outcome: An offline check can detect drift in an archived copy.

techniques.title: Index archived sections by version
techniques.problem: Readers and agents have difficulty finding a particular section in long version history.
techniques.practice: Attach a searchable map to each accepted version and pin its inputs in a receipt.
techniques.outcome: The map can locate an archived section and identify the version it summarizes.

techniques.title: Review the rendered README at two widths
techniques.problem: A Markdown source review misses clipped images and long code blocks.
techniques.practice: Inspect representative desktop and narrow layouts with the opening navigation, images, and commands in view.
techniques.outcome: The reviewer can identify layout failures before publication.

techniques.title: Validate links at the destination path
techniques.problem: Relative links and images may work in the draft folder and break from the homepage.
techniques.practice: Resolve every local destination from the staged publication path and verify its accompanying assets.
techniques.outcome: The homepage links and media still work after relocation.

techniques.title: Test the copy-in path in a clean consumer
techniques.problem: A template can pass its own checks while its documented installation omits required files.
techniques.practice: Exercise the README's copy and initialization steps in a fresh consumer and run the verifier there.
techniques.outcome: The consumer can install and use what the README promises.

techniques.title: Bind merge review to the combined commit
techniques.problem: Passing source-branch checks can go stale when the base or head changes.
techniques.practice: Record both PR parents and the tested combined SHA in the job receipt, then compare them at merge review.
techniques.outcome: The review can establish that the current combination received the checks.

techniques.title: Distinguish intended checks from results
techniques.problem: A catalog of planned checks can look like a record of successful execution.
techniques.practice: Keep the definition or static observation separate from the checkout, environment, and result of a run.
techniques.outcome: Readers can identify which claims have actually been exercised.

techniques.title: Pair a structured inventory with a human guide
techniques.problem: Neither lists of files nor prose alone answer both quick lookup and operating questions.
techniques.practice: Use predictable structured fields for discovery and a short linked guide for interpretation, with a check for consistency.
techniques.outcome: Agents can query records and humans can understand how to apply them.

techniques.title: Put recovery beside the first failed step
techniques.problem: A reader whose first attempt fails has no next step.
techniques.practice: Map recognizable symptoms to safe recovery actions immediately after the tasks that can produce them.
techniques.outcome: A blocked reader can select a concrete recovery action.
